A.explanation: This uses $34 \text{ mm}$ as one fringe width $w$, giving $a$ about 20 times too large. The $34 \text{ mm}$ spans four fringe spacings, not one.

B.explanation: This uses five spacings for five fringes, so $w = 34/5 \text{ mm}$. Five bright fringes contain only four gaps between adjacent maxima.

C.explanation: With $w = 34 \text{ mm}/4 = 8.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, $a = \lambda D/w$ gives about $1.9 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$.

D.explanation: This is about four times too small and follows from miscounting or from inverting $a$ and $w$ in $w = \lambda D/a$.

hints: Look at the 34 mm arrow in the diagram: count how many dark gaps between bright fringes it covers for five marked bright fringes.
Recall the double-slit fringe spacing relation $w = \lambda D / a$, where $w$ is the spacing of one adjacent bright-to-bright interval, $D = 2.4 \text{ m}$ and $\lambda = 680 \text{ nm}$.
First convert $34 \text{ mm}$ to metres and divide by the number of intervals to get $w$, then rearrange to $a = \lambda D / w$ before comparing powers of ten.
walkthrough: Convert the given data to SI units: $\lambda = 680 \text{ nm} = 680 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$, $D = 2.4 \text{ m}$, total measured length $= 34 \text{ mm} = 34 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$.

Find one fringe spacing $w$. The arrow starts and ends on bright fringes and includes five bright fringes, so there are $5 - 1 = 4$ intervals. Hence $w = (34 \times 10^{-3})/4 = 8.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$.
State the governing relation for double-slit interference: fringe spacing $w = \lambda D / a$, where $a$ is the slit separation.
Rearrange for slit separation: $a = \lambda D / w$. Substitute values: $a = (680 \times 10^{-9} \times 2.4)/(8.5 \times 10^{-3})$.
Calculate: numerator $= 1.632 \times 10^{-6}$, then $a = 1.632 \times 10^{-6} / 8.5 \times 10^{-3} = 1.92 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$, about $1.9 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$. This is option C.
